scope: Actual theorem, proof, quartic example and mixed eight-site example as saved in jordan_supplemental.json; author verifier and independent checker replayed.
proof_review: Critical roots cannot be physical sites because p has simple roots. Their multiplicities sum exactly to n−1.

q=1/(w−z_i)−a is analytic with nonzero derivative. Inverse w=z_i+1/(a+q) gives eigenvalue shift exactly q; the off-shell remainder has order m. Taylor coefficients, including the 1/k! convention, therefore satisfy NV_k=V_(k−1).

Within each chain, applying the highest nilpotent power proves independence. Distinct critical roots map injectively to distinct H_i eigenvalues, none equal to the uniform eigenvalue; the total dimension n proves completeness and exact block lengths.
For all H_j, the stated Taylor coefficient c_jl=(−d)^(l−1)/A^(l+1) is correct. c_j1≠0 makes its nilpotent part N times an invertible polynomial, yielding the same Jordan flags and block size.
Hermite interpolation on distinct eigenvalues and all block jets makes every H_j a polynomial in H_i. The minimal polynomial has degree n, giving the Chinese-remainder finite algebra.
The quartic jets and all Hamiltonians were constructed independently in exact Q(i), with rank4 basis and nilpotent ranks2,1,0.
For eight sites, E0=37/60, triple eigenvalue−23/60, p′=4x³(2x⁴−17) and the normalized quartic factor are correct. The four remaining critical roots are simple and distinct from zero.

Final added global operator identity A_j=A_i[I+(z_i−z_j)A_i]⁻¹ is correct on every jet block and uniform vector; denominator eigenvalues are nonzero. The characteristic formula u^n p′(z_i+1/u)/p′(z_i) follows with the stated normalization and has a removable polynomial expansion at u=0.
